rationale: The PLIDA MCD_DTLS_EXT distribution binds mcd_dtls.actv_prtcpn_code to this DSS data element, which publishes a Yes/No/Not required domain.
evidence_quote: Y Yes | N No | NR Not required
supersedes_rationale: The earlier pass did not find the DSS Aristotle data element page, which does publish the codeframe.
variable_description: A flag on a medical or capacity assessment record for whether activity participation requirements applied to the recipient. DSS defines the element as "Indicator of activity participant requirements for a medical assessment", which places it on the assessment rather than on the payment. It sits in the medical conditions detail table with the impairment code and rating, the assessed work capacity and the incapacity period dates, so it qualifies how the assessment was conducted rather than what the person was entitled to.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Activity participant, Code" (item 54207)
value_definition: Three permissible codes — Y for yes, N for no and NR for not required — with a blank as the supplementary missing value. The domain is the DSS permissible value list for the element and carries no other codes.
limitation: It records whether requirements applied, not what the person did. The code says nothing about whether an activity was undertaken, attended, exempted or breached, and it carries neither the hours nor the type of activity. Nor does an NR mean the recipient was excused from mutual obligations generally; it means participation requirements were not relevant to this particular assessment.

rationale: LOC_DERIVED, LOC_DTLS_EXT and LOC_POS_TEMP_TERM_DTLS_EXT all bind addr_prty to this DSS data element, which publishes a four-value priority scale.
evidence_quote: 1 Temporary | 2 Term | 3 Home
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does exist: the DSS Aristotle registry publishes the 1/2/3/5 priority scale.
variable_description: Which of a recipient's concurrently held addresses should be treated as their location on a given day. DSS defines it as a "Derived code highlighting address priority for identifying the location of a recipient on a given day", so it is a tie-breaking rule rather than an observation. On the derived location table it explains why one address episode survived into the geography columns beside it — ARID_HASH_TRUNC, the meshblock and the 2021 ASGS areas — when the person had several addresses recorded at once.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Address priority, Code" (item 54356)
value_definition: A single digit ranking the address types: 1 temporary, 2 term, 3 home, 5 postal or other. The published list has no value 4, and lower numbers take precedence when several address records overlap in time.
limitation: It is a rule for choosing between addresses, not evidence about any one of them. A row carrying priority 3 does not mean the person had no term or postal address, only that the home address won on that day, and the priority says nothing about how long the address was held or how reliable it is — START_DATE and END_DATE carry the duration.

variable_description: What kind of address the recipient supplied on this address detail record — home, postal, temporary, term, business or a nominee's. DSS defines the element as "The type of address given by a recipient". In the address detail table it qualifies POSTCODE, STATE, MESHBLOCK, SA1_MAINCODE and SA2_MAINCODE on the same row, so it decides whether that geography describes where the person lives or only where their mail arrives.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Address type, Code" (item 369)
value_definition: Eight three-letter codes: BUS business, FPO FAO postal, HOM home, NAD nominee, PHY physical, POS postal, TEM temporary and TER term address. The list is the DSS permissible value set for the element.
limitation: A home address type is not proof of residence at the coded meshblock. Nominee and FAO postal addresses belong to a person acting for the recipient, and a business or postal address can be a workplace or a post office, so residential analysis has to filter to HOM or PHY first. MESHMATCH on the same row separately records whether the meshblock came from the address text or from coordinates.

variable_description: The address type carried on the derived location history, the table that gives a recipient one chosen address per period. DSS defines the underlying element as "The type of address given by a recipient". Unlike ADDR_TYPE_CODE in the address detail table, this column describes the address DSS selected for the episode, so it sits with START_DATE, END_DATE, ARID_HASH_TRUNC and the 2021 ASGS geography; POSTALTYPE beside it splits postal addresses further.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Address type, Code" (item 369), bound to the DOMINO derived location table
value_definition: The same DSS address type domain as ADDR_TYPE_CODE, whose three-letter codes include HOM, POS, TEM and TER, although the PLIDA item list publishes no value list against this particular column.

The derived table keeps one address per date range after ADDR_PRTY has been applied, so a type that lost the priority contest never appears here at all. Counting address types in the derived table therefore under-counts the addresses a person actually held, and a person can look like they never had a postal address when they always did.

DSS defines the element as "A code set representing chronological groupings of age of a person". It sits on the point-in-time snapshot table beside AGE, the concession card flags and SNAP_DATE, so it answers what the age profile of the payment population looked like on a chosen day rather than at any event.

evidence_quote: CUR Current | SUS Suspended
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO field codeframe does exist and adds SUS to the generator's CUR-only domain.
variable_description: Whether the benefit episode on this row was current or suspended. DSS defines the element as "The status of a government payment event, as represented by a code". In the benefit detail table it qualifies the episode described by BEN_TYPE_CODE, PERIOD_START_DATE, PERIOD_END_DATE and DURN_DAYS, so it separates a person who was on a payment and receiving it from one who was on it with payment halted.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Benefit status, Code" (item 1502)
value_definition: Two codes only: CUR for current and SUS for suspended. The list carries no cancelled or rejected value, because an episode that ends is closed off by PERIOD_END_DATE with END_RSN_CODE giving the reason.
limitation: A current status does not mean money changed hands. Episodes on a nil rate — where income or assets reduced the entitlement to zero — remain current, and a suspended episode can later be reinstated with arrears backdated across the suspension. Amounts and dates of payment have to come from the payment history tables, not from this flag.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Any Concession Card" (item 108774), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds card_any to a DSS Card element on the Yes/No/Missing value domain, so the field is a Y/N flag for the any concession card. Duplicate code entries were collapsed so each code appears once.
evidence_quote: Y Yes | N No
supersedes_rationale: The exact coding is published: a Y/N flag with N as the default supplementary value.
variable_description: Whether the person held any Centrelink concession card on the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date. DSS defines the element as "Indicates that the person holds any concession cards at this time", so it is a point-in-time rollup rather than a history. It is the summary flag over the individual CARD_ columns on the same snapshot row, and it is the quickest way to identify the concession population without joining the four concession card tables.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Any Concession Card" (item 108774)
value_definition: A yes or no flag taking Y or N, with N registered as the default supplementary value, so a person with no card record reads as N rather than as missing.
limitation: It cannot tell you which card, and the difference matters: a Pensioner Concession Card, a low income Health Care Card and a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card carry very different eligibility and very different concessions. Because N is the default rather than a positive observation, an N is also weak evidence — it can mean no card, or a card whose record did not reach the snapshot.

rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds card_health_care_ech to a DSS Card element on the Yes/No/Missing value domain, so the field is a Y/N flag for the ex-Carer Allowance health care card. Duplicate code entries were collapsed so each code appears once.
evidence_quote: Y Yes | N No
supersedes_rationale: The exact coding is published: a Y/N flag with N as the default supplementary value.
variable_description: Whether the person held the health care card issued to students who were on a Carer Allowance card the day before their 16th birthday. DSS records that the card "can be claimed by 16-25 years old full-time students who were holding a Carer Allowance Health Care Card on the day before their 16th birthday", so this flag marks one specific administrative pathway into a card. On the snapshot table it sits beside CARD_HEALTH_CARE_FST and the other card type flags that CARD_ANY summarises.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Card Health Care Ex-Care Allowance" (item 108747)
value_definition: A Boolean flag one character wide, taking Y or N, evaluated as at the snapshot date rather than over a period.
limitation: It is not a measure of disability or severe illness. The card is not means tested and turns on having held a Carer Allowance card immediately before turning 16, so young people with the same conditions who reached a card by another route, or whose carer's claim lapsed before that date, carry an N. Residence rules also cut in: the card is generally cancelled after six weeks of temporary absence from Australia.

evidence_quote: Y Yes | N No
supersedes_rationale: The exact coding is published: a Y/N flag with N as the default supplementary value.
variable_description: Whether the person held a foster child health care card at the snapshot date. DSS records that "The card is issued only in the name of the child, can only be used to obtain concessions on services used by the child", so the flag belongs to the child being cared for and not to the carer who claimed it. It answers whether a child's health costs were being met through a carer-claimed concession, which is a different question from whether the child's household was on a payment.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Card: Card Health Care Foster" (item 108744)
value_definition: A yes or no flag taking Y or N, held against the child rather than the claiming carer, and true only while the card is current at the snapshot date.
limitation: It does not identify formal foster care or child protection involvement. DSS states the carer "does not need to be a formal foster carer" and that eligibility can cover any child who is not the applicant's natural or adopted child, so grandparent and kinship arrangements sit under the same flag as statutory placements. Using it as an out-of-home-care indicator will over-count substantially.

evidence_quote: 12W Twelve weekly | 1WE Weekly | 2MT Bi-monthly
supersedes_rationale: FTN is not in the published domain; the fortnightly code is 2WE, and DSS publishes all 15 frequency codes.
variable_description: How often the CDEP income recorded on this row was received. DSS defines the element as "The frequency of income received by a client for participation in Community Development Employment Projects (CDEP)". It qualifies CDEP_DLY_INC, the daily income amount, and sits beside EMPLYR_ID and the event start and end dates, so it says at what interval the underlying payment reached the participant before DSS converted it to a daily figure.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: CDEP income frequency, Code" (item 547)

The income beside it is already expressed as a daily amount, so this code must not be used to re-annualise the figure, and having two quarterly codes means a naive grouping by code splits the same interval in two. CDEP was progressively wound up and replaced by remote employment programs, so the absence of rows in later years is a program change rather than missing data.

supersedes_rationale: CMTY_CODE is not an SA2 code: it is a four-character Centrelink community code, and DSS publishes the full list.

DSS defines the element as "Community code for an Australian address". On the derived location table it sits with the ASGS meshblock, SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns for the same address episode, so it is an operational place name running in parallel with the statistical geography rather than a substitute for it.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Australian community, Code" (item 682)
value_definition: Four-character codes over a published list of about 8,460 permissible values, such as ALIE for Alice Springs, ABAY for Apollo Bay and OAND for Old Andado. Most are alphabetic, but a numbered suffix separates repeated place names, as in BLH1, BLH2 and BLH3 for Black Hill. The list is a Centrelink operational geography and is not part of any ABS classification.

The list covers ordinary towns and cities alongside remote communities, so it cannot be filtered to identify residents of discrete Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities; RMT_IND in the address detail table and the ASGS remoteness structure are the fields for that. Codes are also not mutually exclusive with postcodes and cannot be aggregated to any published statistical area.

description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Caree: Medical condition(s), Code" (item 84500)

The groups are broad, one caree can carry several rows at once, and PFC and UNK absorb cases the grouping cannot place, so condition prevalence estimated from this column will not match health system counts and cannot be compared with hospital or Medicare data.

DSS defines the element as "The type of rent paid by a recipient, as represented by a code" and adds that for board and lodging, "Board means that some regular meals are provided. Lodging means no meals are provided." It qualifies HSE_WK_RENT, because government rent and free board attract no assistance while private rent does.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Household: Rent type, Code" (item 205)
value_definition: A three-letter code, format AAA, from a 16-value list. It distinguishes private rent (PRI) from government rent (GOV) and other housing organisations (OHO), the board and lodging arrangements (BOA, LOD, FBD, FBL, FLD), and non-standard payments such as SIT site fees, MOO mooring fees, MNT nursing home or retirement village maintenance and RSP respite fees, with NRP for no rent paid.
limitation: It classifies the payment, not the dwelling or the landlord, so a person renting privately from a relative and one renting through an agent share a code. A GOV value marks a payment treated as government rent under the rules and is not a public housing tenancy record, and the amount beside it is the figure the person reported rather than a verified rent.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Impairment: Impairment Rating, Code XX" (item 65080), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT binds imprmt_code to "Impairment: Impairment Rating, Code XX", an impairment rating in five-point steps from 0 to 95 plus NA.
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does define the scale: it is a 0-95 impairment rating, not a 1-3 improvement code.
variable_description: The impairment rating given to a medical condition at a Disability Support Pension assessment. DSS defines it as "The code that represents the level to which a medical condition is assessed as having an impact on normal functions as related to work performance", scored against the Social Security (Tables for the Assessment of Work-related Impairment for Disability Support Pension) Determination 2011. It sits with IMPRMT_RATE and IMPRMT_VER_DATE, and with MED_PRMY_GRP, which names the condition the rating applies to.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Impairment: Impairment Rating, Code XX" (item 65080)
value_definition: A two-character code, format XX, carrying a points score in five-point steps from 0 to 95, plus NA. The determination assigns 0 points for no functional impact, 5 mild, 10 moderate, 20 severe and 30 extreme within each table, so recorded scores are totals across the tables assessed.
limitation: A rating is not a diagnosis and not a measure of how serious the condition is; it scores work-related functional impact under one determination, and ratings made under the earlier impairment tables are not on the same basis as those made under the 2011 Determination. Twenty points is the qualifying threshold for the pension, so the distribution clusters there for administrative reasons rather than clinical ones.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Education institution type, Code" (item 733), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: EDU_DTLS_EXT and EDU_FTB_EXT bind inst_type to "Course: Education institution type, Code", nine single-letter institution types.
evidence_quote: B Both Primary and Secondary | H Higher Education Private Providers |
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these institution codes.
variable_description: The kind of institution the student attends, from primary school to university. DSS defines the element as one that "Identifies the type of institution at which the student is studying", so it describes the provider while COURSE_LVL describes the level of study. The codeframe keeps TAFEs and private higher education providers separate from universities, a distinction that matters to Family Tax Benefit and student payment rules.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Education institution type, Code" (item 733)
value_definition: A single letter, format A, with nine values: P primary school, S secondary school, B both primary and secondary, O special school, T TAFE, U university, Q higher education TAFEs, H higher education private providers and R private provider.
limitation: It names no institution, sector funding or location, so it cannot be used to study particular providers or to link to higher education collections. Provider type and course level can also disagree, since a TAFE can deliver a degree, so it is no substitute for COURSE_LVL.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Status Code" (item 108850), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds isp_ben_status to "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Status Code", published as CUR and SUS with NA.
evidence_quote: CUR Current | SUS Suspicious
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these benefit-status codes.
variable_description: The state of the person's income support payment at the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date. DSS gives the definition as "Income support payment status" and says the field "displays the customers entitlement to ISP", with the payment itself named in ISP_TYPE_CODE. ISP_ACTIVE_START_DATE, ISP_ACTIVE_END_DATE and ISP_PANEL_DAYS on the same row bound the active spell this status describes.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Status Code" (item 108850)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, with CUR and SUS as permissible values and N as the default. The registry labels SUS "Suspicious", which reads as a typographical error for suspended.
limitation: It is a state on one day, not an outcome: suspensions are frequently restored within days, so counting SUS records as exits from income support overstates them. The status attaches to whichever payment ISP_TYPE_CODE names, so it cannot be used to follow one payment across a transfer to another.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Type Code" (item 108851), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds isp_type_code to "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Type Code", 22 income support payment mnemonics plus NA.
evidence_quote: ABA Abstudy - Schooling Applicant | ABY Abstudy | AGE Age Pension
supersedes_rationale: Field-level equivalence is publicly verified by the PLIDA column binding in the DSS registry.
variable_description: Which income support payment the person was on at the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date. DSS defines it as a "Code indicating which Income Support Payment was received", and PREV_ISP and NEXT_ISP on the same row give the payments either side, which makes payment-to-payment transitions readable without joining the episode tables. FIRST_ACTIVE_ISP and LAST_ACTIVE_ISP mark the ends of the active spell.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Income Support Payment: ISP Type Code" (item 108851)
value_definition: A code of up to four characters, format AAA{A}, from a 22-value list of payment mnemonics plus NA. It names pensions (AGE, DSP, CAR, WID, WFA, WFD), allowances (JSP, NSA, PTA, SKA, SPL, WDA, BVA), parenting payments (PPS, PPP) and student payments (ABY, ABA, AUS, YLS, YLO, YLA).
limitation: It holds income support only, so family payments, Rent Assistance, supplements and concession cards are absent and sit in their own blocks on the same row. Superseded and current payment names also coexist, with NSA and JSP either side of the March 2020 change, so a time series needs those pairs collapsed.

rationale: EDU_LVL_EXT binds lvl_attained to "Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Code", a 28-value DSS attainment codeframe (not ASCED).
evidence_quote: ADP Advanced Diploma | ASD Associate Diploma | BAC Bachelor's Degree
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does exist; it is a DSS-specific attainment list rather than an ASCED crosswalk.
variable_description: The highest completed level of education Centrelink holds for the person. DSS says the element "Refers to completed education, not a current course of study being undertaken by a recipient" and that "The most recent level of educational attainment is recorded", which makes edu_lvl the attainment table and edu_ftb and edu_dtls the enrolment tables. STDNT_STS_CODE on the same row gives the person's study status when the attainment was recorded.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Code" (item 703)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, from a 28-value DSS attainment list. It runs U10 less than Year 10 and Y10 to Y13, certificates C01 to C04, then ASD, DIP, ADP, BAC, HNR, MST, PGR and DOC, with TRA trade qualification, HEB bridging course, UGR undergraduate, UNK unknown, and several entries marked no longer valid.
limitation: It is neither ASCED nor the Census attainment items, so it will not concord to ABS education counts without a mapping. Attainment is recorded when Centrelink has a reason to ask, so it is absent for people never assessed for a study-related payment and can be years out of date for people who qualified after their last assessment.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Text" (item 51677), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column; the element is the text representation of the same value domain (item 83) used by LVL_ATTAINED
rationale: EDU_LVL_EXT binds lvl_attained_desc to "Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Text", which implements the same value domain as LVL_ATTAINED; the labels shown are the published meanings, and the text column is expected to carry the label rather than the code. Adversarial verification could not confirm this mapping against the cited source, so the domain is recorded as inferred rather than published. The values are recorded as the label set rather than code-and-label pairs, because this column holds the description while LVL_ATTAINED holds the code.
supersedes_rationale: The labels are source-verified through the shared value domain, though the registry does not state whether the column stores the label or the code.
variable_description: The text form of the attainment level held as a code in LVL_ATTAINED on the same row. DSS defines the element as "The level of educational attainment of a recipient represented as text", so the two columns express one value domain, one as a code and one as its label. Carrying both is a convenience of the extract rather than two separate facts about the person.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Level of educational attainment, Text" (item 51677)
value_definition: A string carrying the label of the attainment level, such as Bachelor's Degree, Certificate 3, Year 12 or Trade Qualification. The set matches the 28 labels behind LVL_ATTAINED, including those marked no longer valid, with a no-value label where attainment is not recorded.
limitation: Being a label rather than a code, joins and grouping are exposed to punctuation and casing, so Bachelor's Degree with an apostrophe will not match Bachelors Degree. Prefer LVL_ATTAINED for any tabulation, and treat this column as display text.

rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT binds man_code to "Recipient: Manifestly disabled, Code", a 14-value list naming the manifest grant ground.
evidence_quote: APP Successful Appeal | BLI Permanent Blindness | HV4 Category 4 HIV
supersedes_rationale: The code meaning is published: it names the manifest grant ground (blindness, terminal illness, nursing home level of care and so on), not a Y/N flag.
variable_description: The ground on which Disability Support Pension was granted without a full impairment assessment. DSS defines the element as "A code describing the manifest disability of the recipient", covering manifest grants such as permanent blindness, terminal illness or a nursing home level of care. Its presence on a record explains why IMPRMT_CODE and the medical condition groups can be sparse on the same assessment.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Manifestly disabled, Code" (item 629)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, from a 14-value list. It names the manifest ground (BLI permanent blindness, TRM terminal illness, INT intellectual disability, HV4 category 4 HIV or AIDS, NHM nursing home level of care, TPI special rate or Military Rehabilitation Act) and the outcomes MCW, MDI, MNI, MWK and MWL that record a manifest claim not accepted.
limitation: It is a claim-processing pathway, not a diagnosis or a severity ranking, so a person with a serious condition assessed the usual way carries nothing here. Several codes record an unsuccessful manifest test while reading like conditions, so treating every non-blank value as a manifest grant overstates the count.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Primary medical condition group, Code" (item 107942), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT binds med_prmy_grp to "Recipient: Primary medical condition group, Code", 23 three-letter DSS medical condition groups.
evidence_quote: ABI Acquired Brain Impairment | AMP Amputation | CAN Cancer/Tumour
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm the medical-group abbreviations.
variable_description: The broad group of the main medical condition recorded at a Disability Support Pension medical assessment. DSS defines the element as "A recipient's primary medical condition, as represented by a code" and notes it is a high level grouping produced through a concordance rather than a code the assessor typed. MED_SCNDRY_GRP holds the same grouping for a second condition, and IMPRMT_CODE holds the rating attached to the assessment.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Primary medical condition group, Code" (item 107942)
value_definition: A three-letter code, format AAA, from a 23-value condition group list. Groups follow body systems and impairment types, including MUS musculo-skeletal and connective tissue, PSY psychological or psychiatric, CIR circulatory, NER nervous system, INT intellectual or learning and CAN cancer or tumour, with PFC poorly defined cause and UNK for grants made before 12 November 1991.
limitation: It is an aggregation, not a diagnosis: no ICD code sits behind it in the extract, so conditions within a group cannot be separated. Records exist only where a medical assessment took place, so the column describes assessed claimants rather than disability across the DOMINO population.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Secondary medical condition group, Code" (item 107944), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: MCD_DTLS_EXT binds med_scndry_grp to "Recipient: Secondary medical condition group, Code", which shares the 23-value medical condition group domain.
evidence_quote: ABI Acquired Brain Impairment | AMP Amputation | CAN Cancer/Tumour
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm the medical-group abbreviations.
variable_description: The condition group for a second medical condition recorded at the same assessment as MED_PRMY_GRP. DSS defines it as "A recipient's secondary medical condition represented at a higher level of aggregation" using the primary condition's groups, so the two columns are directly comparable. MED_SCNDRY_ID and MED_SCNDRY_PERM beside it identify the secondary condition record and mark whether it is permanent.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Secondary medical condition group, Code" (item 107944)
value_definition: A three-letter code, format AAA, sharing the 23-value medical condition group domain used by MED_PRMY_GRP, so the same group codes appear with the same meanings on both columns.
limitation: A blank means no secondary condition was recorded at that assessment, which is not evidence of a single condition, and any third or later condition has nowhere to go in this structure. Primary and secondary also reflect the assessment's ordering for payment purposes, not which condition affects the person most.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Principal Carer Reason, Code" (item 54745), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: CIR_PRIN_CAR_EXT binds nspp_prcpl_carer_rsn_code to "Recipient: Principal Carer Reason, Code", a four-value list.
evidence_quote: NDE No dependent children | PCC Partner is principal carer | NPC
supersedes_rationale: The codes are published rather than locally inferred.
variable_description: Why the person is not treated as the principal carer of a dependent child. DSS records the element as one "used to record Principal Carer reason value", and every published code is a negative ground, so it explains the absence of the status that PRINCIPAL_PARENT_IND on the same row flags. Principal carer status changes participation requirements and payment rates, which is why the reason is kept at all.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Principal Carer Reason, Code" (item 54745)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, with a four-value published list: NDE no dependent children, PCC partner is principal carer, NPC not principal carer, and a blank.
limitation: It cannot confirm that someone is a principal carer, since the codes name reasons they are not, so both presence and absence have to be read against PRINCIPAL_PARENT_IND. It also names no child and gives no count, so it does not stand in for the family composition tables.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Address type, Code" (item 369), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column; in practice the postal-type column is likely to carry the postal subset of these codes, which the registry does not state
rationale: The LOC_DERIVED (PLIDA) distribution binds loc_derived.postaltype to "Address: Address type, Code"; the published domain is the general eight-value address type list. Adversarial verification could not confirm this mapping against the cited source, so the domain is recorded as inferred rather than published.
supersedes_rationale: The DSS Aristotle registry publishes the address type code table for this column.
variable_description: What kind of postal address the loc_derived record is. The DSS element bound to this column defines address type as "The type of address given by a recipient", and on loc_derived it sits beside ADR_TYP, so one column carries the address's role and this one its postal variety. The address itself is represented by ARID_HASH_TRUNC and the ASGS geography columns on the same row.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Address: Address type, Code" (item 369)
value_definition: A three-letter code, format AAA, from the DSS eight-value address type list: HOM home, POS postal, BUS business, PHY physical, TEM temporary, TER term, NAD nominee and FPO. The registry does not publish which subset a postal-type column carries, so the recorded domain is the general list.
limitation: It describes the address record, not where anyone lives: a postal address can be a post office box, an agent or a nominee, so a row typed here is not evidence of residence. Because the postal subset is unpublished, an unexpected code should be checked against ADR_TYP rather than treated as an error.

variable_description: Why this concession card was issued or reissued. DSS defines the element as the "Reason why a client has requested a concession card issue/ reissue/ interim voucher issue", so most values describe card production rather than a change in entitlement. It pairs with CARD_ISSUE_DATE, and the same 46-value list serves all four card tables.

rationale: RLT_CUST_PTNR_LIST, RLT_PARENT_CHILD_LIST and RLT_GRAND_PARENT_CHILD_LIST bind rel_code to "Recipient: Relationship type, Code", a 16-value list.
evidence_quote: CHI Child | DEF Defacto | DIV Divorced
supersedes_rationale: A public relationship codeframe does exist in the DSS Aristotle registry.
variable_description: How the person is related to the linked person identified in EXT_DOM_REL_ID. DSS defines the element as "The type of relationship the client has to another recipient, as represented by a code", and the table fixes the kind of link: partner on rlt_cust_ptnr_list, parent and child or grandparent and grandchild on the other relationship tables. REL_QUAL_CODE qualifies the same link where a couple is living apart.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Relationship type, Code" (item 375)
value_definition: A three-letter code, format AAA, from a 16-value list. It carries couple statuses (MAR married, DEF de facto, REG registered, SEP separated, DIV divorced, WID widow, SIN single) and family roles (PAR parent, CHI child, GPA grandparent, GCH grandchild, SIB sibling, GAU guardian, WAR ward), with NRE not required and UNK unknown.
limitation: It records the relationship Centrelink assessed for payment purposes, not the household: partners under the income test can live apart, and people living together need not be recorded as a couple. The link also runs only to another person known to Centrelink, so relatives outside the payment system leave no row at all.

They cover illness separation (ILS, ILB, ILC, ILP), separation under one roof (SUR), temporary separation (TEM, TEB, TEC, TEP), custody and care settings (GAC, GAO, PIJ, REC, REP, PMH, PSC, PSY), overseas cases (OVC, OVP) and historical statuses such as DES deserted wife and S24 provisions.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Status Code" (item 108843), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds rent_ben_status to "Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Status Code", published as CUR with N as default.
evidence_quote: CUR Current
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm this benefit-status code.
variable_description: Whether Rent Assistance entitlement was current at the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date. The DSS entry points the reader to "the Rent Assistance recipient status" and publishes CUR as the only permissible value with a default beside it, so the column works as a presence flag on the snapshot day. RENT_TYPE_CODE names the payment the assistance was attached to, and RENT_PANEL_DAYS gives days active.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Status Code" (item 108843)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, holding CUR for current with N as the supplementary default where no Rent Assistance entitlement applies.
limitation: It carries no dollar amount and no rent, so it cannot measure housing costs or the value of assistance received; hh_hse_dtls holds the reported rent. Rent Assistance is also paid on rent above a threshold and up to a maximum, so a current flag says nothing about whether the maximum rate applied.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Type Code" (item 108844), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds rent_type_code to "Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Type Code", five Rent Assistance stream mnemonics plus NA.
evidence_quote: RAG Rent Assistance Parenting | RAP Rent Assistance Pension | RAF Rent
supersedes_rationale: The mnemonics are published in the DSS registry with the PLIDA column binding.
variable_description: Which payment the person's Rent Assistance was attached to at the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date. Rent Assistance is not a payment in its own right but a supplement added to a pension, allowance, family payment or student payment, and this column names that host stream. Read it with RENT_BEN_STATUS for whether the entitlement was current, and with the income support and Family Tax Benefit blocks for the underlying payment.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Rent Assistance: RENT Type Code" (item 108844), read against the Snap-DOMINO (PLIDA) distribution
value_definition: A code of up to four characters, format AAA{A}, with five stream values — RAP pension, RAN Newstart-type allowance, RAF family, RAG parenting and RAS Abstudy — plus NA where no Rent Assistance applies.
limitation: The stream follows the payment the supplement rode on, so a person whose base payment changed appears to change Rent Assistance type with no change in their housing at all. Assistance paid with Family Tax Benefit is a family entitlement, so RAF on one person's record is not evidence of a payment made to that person.

value_definition: Free text of up to ten characters, format A{10}. The registry publishes no code list, so the values are short uppercase tokens taken from the entitlement determination the row came from rather than entries in a closed classification.
limitation: With no published list, an analysis has to derive the distinct values from the data and cannot tell a new entitlement class from a data error. The tokens are also table specific, so the same string need not carry the same meaning on the Abstudy and Pensioner Education Supplement tables.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Student participation status, Code" (item 710), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: EDU_DTLS_EXT and EDU_FTB_EXT bind stdnt_prtcpn_sts to "Course: Student participation status, Code", a 44-value list.
evidence_quote: APC Access program | API Apprentice - INC only | APL Apprentice
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these student-status codes.
variable_description: How the student is participating in the course on this row: full time, part time, apprentice, or exempt from study for a listed reason. DSS defines the element as one that "Refers to the current participation status of a student", and on edu_ftb it is the test that decides whether a child counts as a student for Family Tax Benefit. STDNT_START_DATE and STDNT_END_DATE bound the period the status covers.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Student participation status, Code" (item 710)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, from a 44-value list. It carries study load (FTS full time, PTS part time, U25, U50, O50 and the concessional loads C25, C50, C66), apprenticeship and traineeship codes (APT, API, APL), intention to study (INS, INT), and exemption grounds such as HOM homelessness, INP incapacity, MPC major personal crisis, CAR caring responsibilities and LRD learning difficulty.
limitation: It is a payment status, not attendance: a full-time code means the person met the load test at the time, not that they attended class. The exemption codes describe circumstances accepted as reasons for not studying, so treating them as study statuses puts non-students into the student count.

rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds sup_ben_status to "Payment: SUPPLEMENTARY: SUP Status Code", published as CUR and SUS with N as default.
evidence_quote: CUR Current | SUS Suspicious
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these benefit-status codes.
variable_description: Whether a supplementary payment entitlement was current at the Snap-DOMINO snapshot date. The DSS registry says the field "displays the customers entitlement to SUP", with SUP_TYPE_CODE naming which supplementary payment is meant. SUP_ON_SNAP and SUP_PANEL_DAYS on the same row give receipt on the day and days active over the panel period.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: SUPPLEMENTARY: SUP Status Code" (item 108837)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, with CUR and SUS as permissible values and N as the default. As on the income support status column, the registry labels SUS "Suspicious", which reads as a typographical error for suspended.
limitation: One status covers the single supplementary payment the record names, so a person receiving two supplements is represented once and the second is invisible here. A current status also carries no amount, which the snapshot does not hold for supplementary payments at all.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Supplementary Type Code" (item 108833), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: SNAP_DOMINO_BETA_EXT binds sup_type_code to "Payment: Supplementary Type Code", seven supplementary payment mnemonics plus NA.
evidence_quote: YTA Youth Training Allowance | EIC Assistance for Isolated Children | EPA
supersedes_rationale: Field-level equivalence is publicly verified by the PLIDA column binding.
variable_description: Which supplementary payment the Snap-DOMINO supplementary block describes. Supplementary payments sit outside income support and family payments — Carer Allowance, Double Orphan Pension, Parental Leave Pay, Assistance for Isolated Children and the education supplements — so this column says which of them the status and duration fields beside it refer to. Read it with SUP_BEN_STATUS and SUP_PANEL_DAYS.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Supplementary Type Code" (item 108833), read against the Snap-DOMINO (PLIDA) distribution
value_definition: A code of up to four characters, format AAA{A}, with seven payment values — CDA Carer Allowance, DOP Double Orphan Pension, PPL Parental Leave Pay, DAP Dad and Partner Pay, EIC Assistance for Isolated Children, EPA Pensioner Education Supplement for Abstudy and YTA Youth Training Allowance — plus NA.
limitation: The list is not the full set of Australian supplementary payments, so a blank is not proof the person received none, and payments such as Rent Assistance have their own block on the same row. Where more than one supplement is held, only one can be named here.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Task, Code" (item 577), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: INC_UNE_VAR_EXT binds task_code to "Recipient: Task, Code", nine assessment task codes.
evidence_quote: ABY ABY Assess Action | AIC Isolated Children | CMP Compensation Income
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these task codes.
variable_description: Which assessment task produced the unearned income figure on this row. DSS defines the element as one that "Holds the task code for an assessment" and notes that it "Refers to the variable TASK_CODE in the DOMINO longitudinal data set", so it names the kind of income assessed behind UNE_DLY_INC_VAR — compensation, superannuation, a foreign pension, another government payment. It is the only column on inc_une_var that says what the income actually is.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Recipient: Task, Code" (item 577)
value_definition: A three-letter code, format AAA, with nine values: CMP compensation income, SUP superannuation, FIN foreign income or pension, OGP other government payment, OIN other income, EAN earnings, ABY Abstudy assessment action, AIC Assistance for Isolated Children and PES Pensioner Education Supplement.
limitation: It is a Centrelink assessment task, not an income source classification, so economically different receipts fall together under OIN other income and cannot be separated. Only income that mattered to an assessment is recorded, so the table is not a measure of the person's total unearned income.

description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Course: Education field of study, Code" (item 725), read against the ABS PLIDA DOMINO data item list
value_definition: A three-letter code, format AAA, from the DSS 111-value education field of study list, the same domain COURSE_TYPE uses, with entries such as ACC accounting, APF full time apprenticeship, DRA drafting and BTH beauty therapy.

The column also records nothing about the apprenticeship's stage, employer or outcome; the date columns bound the episode and no completion flag is carried.

value_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Benefit Zero Pay Reason, Code" (item 54741), bound to the DOMINO (External PLIDA Version) distribution column
rationale: DET_BEN_ZERO_PAY_EXT binds zero_pay_rsn to "Payment: Benefit Zero Pay Reason, Code", a 48-value list.
evidence_quote: API Awaiting Participation Interview | ARC Awaiting RapidConnect Compliance | ASS Assets
supersedes_rationale: A public DOMINO code table does confirm these zero-payment reason codes.
variable_description: Why a benefit that remained current paid nothing for this period. DSS defines the element plainly as "This is the reason the rate went to zero", which makes det_ben_zero_pay the table that separates a nil rate from a cancellation: entitlement continues, the rate does not. BEN_TYPE names the payment and the period dates bound the nil-rate spell.
description_source: DSS Aristotle Metadata Registry, data element "Payment: Benefit Zero Pay Reason, Code" (item 54741)
value_definition: A three-character code, format XXX, from a 48-value list. Reasons run from income and assets (INC excess income, ITH income too high, ASS assets over limit, ATT asset taper, EAN earnings preclude payment), through maintenance and compensation periods (IMP, IMN, CMP), to compliance penalties (BCH non-payment penalty, TCF targeted compliance framework) and overlaps with other payments (PLA and PLB Parental Leave Pay, CDP CDEP, RCC regular care children).
limitation: A zero-pay row is still a period of entitlement, so dropping it treats someone on income support as off it, while counting it as a payment overstates dollars received. The reason is the rule that produced the nil rate, not the person's income: earnings, a partner's earnings and a compensation preclusion each have their own code and none carries an amount.
